title: Even or odd
prompt:
Write a function `parity(n: i32) -> String` that returns `"even"` if `n` is even and `"odd"` if it is odd.

```text
parity(4)  -> even
parity(7)  -> odd
parity(-3) -> odd
```

Zero and negative numbers count too.

run.output:
even
odd
even
odd
even
odd

hints: The remainder operator is `%`. `n % 2` is 0 for even numbers.
Careful with negatives: in Rust `-3 % 2` is `-1`, not `1`. So compare with `0`, not with `1`.
Use `if n % 2 == 0 { ... } else { ... }`. Text values can be made with `String::from("even")` or `"even".to_string()`.
explanation: `n % 2 == 0` works for negative numbers too, because `-8 % 2` is `0`. Checking `n % 2 == 1` would wrongly call `-3` even, since `-3 % 2` is `-1`.
